summary.text: Russ Fulcher is the Republican U.S. Representative for Idaho's 1st District, serving since January 2019, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

A fourth-generation Idahoan who grew up on a dairy farm in Meridian, he worked about 24 years in the technology industry before ten years in the Idaho Senate, and he sits on the House Energy and Commerce and Natural Resources committees.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, Fulcher is a fourth-generation Idahoan who grew up on a dairy farm in Meridian, Idaho, and graduated from Meridian High School. He earned bachelor's and master's degrees in business from Boise State University (in 1984 and 1988, according to Ballotpedia) and additional certifications in electronic engineering.
He spent 24 years in the high-technology industry, working for Micron Technology and Preco Electronics, and his official biography says he did business in 60 countries.

Fulcher served in the Idaho Senate for 10 years, six of them as Majority Caucus Chair, and sat on the Senate State Affairs and Education committees. His official biography describes Idaho's grocery tax credit as his signature legislation there and says it has returned about $800 million to Idaho families.
While still a state senator he ran for the Republican nomination for governor in 2014; Ballotpedia lists that primary as a defeat.
Fulcher won the U.S. House seat for Idaho's 1st District in 2018, succeeding Raul Labrador, and was re-elected in 2020, 2022, and 2024.

He won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election with 64.3% of the vote to Kaylee Peterson's 28.8%, Sarah Zabel's 6.1% and Brendan Gomez's 0.9%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
He sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee and the Natural Resources Committee and previously served on the Education and the Workforce Committee.
